why: Commits 1 and 2 are deletions named line by line (next.config.ts lines 7, 8 and 113, legacyModule at 59/90/100/110, the two setters), and the type check, unit tests, int tests and e2e catch a leftover reference. Commit 3 is the risky part. It writes a custom migration that copies three demo function bodies out of the baseline and edits them, replaces the features trigger, rewrites modules on every store row and narrows a check constraint. It also edits about twenty test expectations, and it must not be pushed until commit 2 is live, an ordering no check enforces.
harm_if_wrong: A mis-copied demo function or trigger, or commit 3 pushed in the same deploy as commit 2, would make writes to commerce.stores (feature switches, new stores, demo content) fail in production on the narrowed check while CI passed.
brief_problems: The three lines to replace in each add_demo function are indented in the baseline ('     SET modules = …', '   WHERE id = p_store;'); the brief quotes them unindented, so an exact-text search by the cheap model may miss them.
'Push this commit only after the second commit is live' sits inside one change's how rather than as a stop or a separate push, and nothing in the checks catches a combined push.
